newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end at record closing high.

text.p: *Stocks ended at a record close after the Dow continued its record run Friday. Volume 319.2 million shares, value A$544.9 million, 1,125 stocks traded, 349 steady, 410 up, 366 down.
Australian shares finished at a record close on Monday after rising modestly from the open following the continued strength of the Dow which achieved another record high close on Friday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 11.3 points higher at 2,394.7, two points higher than its previous record close of 2,392.7 set on Thursday last week.
The December share price index ended one point lower at 2,405 and at a 10.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Volume was thin and dealers said a lack of company news resulted in low activity from disinterested investors.
"It was always going to be stronger today - the banks and resource sectors led the market again," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney firm, Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said the 2400 level was still proving to be a significant barrier for the market.
"I think stronger base metal prices combined with a weaker local currency would help the market past this level," he said.

National Australia Bank was the most outstanding blue chip issue on the day, its stock topping the turnover list and finishing 22 cents higher at A$14.55 after touching an all-time high of A$14.59 during the session.

In other markets, Australian bonds weakened after a third quarter capital expenditure report came in stronger than expected. Capital expenditure rose a seasonally adjusted 0.9 percent in the September quarter compared with median forecasts for a 3.0 percent fall.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.09 percent, up 0.04 percentage point from Friday's closing level.
The Australian dollar ended slightly weaker on profit-taking following the unit's strong rise last week.
At 4.40 p.m. (0540 GMT), the unit was quoted at USD$0.8108/13.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trading remained thin with activity slightly busier than Friday's quiet session.
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 5,124 (5,055)

Blue chip resource issues underpinned market gains despite softer base and precious metal prices on Friday.
Gold issues slipped after price of gold weakened on Friday.
Banks pushed ahead and bolstered the industrial sector.
Company raised estimated capital cost of the Hartley platinum mine in Zimbabwe.
